parts:
Hi Steve,

I suggest consulting a good book, like "Camera Traps in Animal
Ecology" (http://www.amazon.com/Camera-Traps-Animal-Ecology-Analyses/dp/4431994947),
if you have not yet done so. You raise too many issues to address in
an brief email, but I wish you the best of luck with your research.

Richard

On Tue, Apr 23, 2013 at 3:59 AM, Steve Ross <steve...@bristol.ac.uk> wrote:
> Dear All,
>
> I hope this question is within the remit of the group, I am having
> difficulty finding publications using similar designs. I am conducting
> camera trapping surveys for the Arabian tahr (non-migratory ungulate) across
> a 30,000 km2 mountainous landscape. The projects main objective is to create
> predictive distribution models and gain understanding of factors affecting
> large scale distrubution to guide conservation management of the species at
> the landscape scale.
>
> Due to the large sample area and terrain we plan to take 2-3 years to survey
> 150 randomly selected sites with 450 camera traps. Cameras will be set for
> 90 days allowing detection to be calculated, but will then be removed, to
> reduce effort and increase spatial coverage, so inerseasonal occupancy will
> not be known. I have completed a season of pilot work and initial results
> suggest the cameras have good detection probabilities when the species is
> present.
>
> Does anyone know of studies with similar objectives, at similar scales and
> using open season designs, or does anyone have advice to offer in terms of
> improving the design and analyses of the dataset? If the current design
> won't work analytically then I see the alternative options to either split
> the area into 3 and calculate occupancy and distribution using 3 separate
> standard closed season models, or try and continue sampling at a portion of
> the sites (say 20) to allow seasonal effects to be measured.
>
> I'd appreciate any thoughts or advice
>
> Thanks, Steve
>
